'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
***[[Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan (2021)|Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan]]
****[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] announces that the [[United States]] will end its military mission in [[Afghanistan]] by August 31. Also, [[White House Press Secretary]] [[Jen Psaki]] says that the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] will evacuate Afghan interpreters from the country. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/07/08/us-military-mission-in-afghanistan-will-end-by-august-31-biden-says-.html (CNBC)] [https://www.politico.com/news/2021/07/08/us-evacuate-afghan-interpreters-next-month-498807 (Politico)]
***[[Afghanistan–Tajikistan relations]]
****[[Taliban]] spokesperson Mohammad Suhail Shaheen says that the organization does not plan to attack the [[Afghanistan–Tajikistan border|Afghan–Tajik border]]. [https://tass.com/world/1312057 (TASS)]
***Sixty-nine Taliban fighters are killed during clashes with the [[Politics of Afghanistan|government]] in the town of [[Qala e Naw]], [[Badghis Province|Badghis]]. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/south-asia/69-taliban-terrorists-killed-23-injured-as-afghan-forces-regain-control-of-qala-e-naw-city/articleshow/84228756.cms (''The Times of India'')]
***[[British Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] is set to outline the plan for the final withdrawal of British troops from Afghanistan in detail. [https://apnews.com/article/afghanistan-europe-government-and-politics-c0cec98b6a2d2279548cfb9e1bcdc499 (AP)]
*[[Assassination of Jovenel Moïse]]
**Three of the [[assassin]]s of [[President of Haiti|Haitian President]] [[Jovenel Moïse]], who was killed yesterday, are shot dead during a shootout with police in [[Port-au-Prince]]. Seventeen others are arrested, while six more are on the run. The attackers are identified as 26 Colombian [[mercenaries]] and two American-Haitians. The masterminds of the assassination and motive behind the assassination are unknown. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-57766749 (BBC News)]
*[[2021 Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan clashes|2021 Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan conflict]]
**A [[Kyrgyzstan]] [[border guard]] is killed during clashes at the [[Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan border]]. [https://akipress.com/news:660347:Kyrgyz_border_guard_killed_in_attack_on_border_with_Tajikistan/ (AKIPress)]
*American diplomats and troops in [[Iraq]] and [[Syria]] are targeted in three rocket and [[Unmanned aerial vehicle|drone]] attacks in the past 24 hours, including at least 14 rockets hitting an Iraqi airbase, wounding two American soldiers. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/8/rockets-fired-at-us-embassy-in-iraq-after-series-of-attacks (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Rupganj factory fire]]
**At least 52 people are killed and about 30 others injured by a fire in a [[food processing]] factory in [[Rupganj Upazila|Rupganj]], [[Narayanganj District|Narayanganj]], [[Dhaka Division]], [[Bangladesh]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/9/deadly-fire-at-bangladesh-food-processing-factory (Al Jazeera)]
* A [[Richter scale|magnitude]] 5.9 M<sub>L</sub> [[earthquake]] strikes south of [[Lake Tahoe]], near the [[California]]–[[Nevada]] state border, triggering a series of strong aftershocks. Though resulting in minimal damage and no casualties, it is the largest quake to hit the region in nearly 25 years. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/us/magnitude-5-9-earthquake-shakes-up-california-nevada-border-regionally-largest-in-almost-two-and-a-half-decades/ar-AALWyrd?ocid=uxbndlbing (USA Today)]


'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record for the fourth consecutive day of 38,391 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2.41 million. [https://news.yahoo.com/indonesia-sees-record-38-391-102414477.html (Yahoo! News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Israel]] reports its first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant]] in a vaccinated woman who returned to the country from abroad. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/first-case-of-delta-plus-covid-variant-found-in-israel-report/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 135 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 5,903. The country also surpasses 800,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/covid-19-malaysia-8868-new-cases-lockdown-record-135-deaths-15180050 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports a record 1,275 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 164,028. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/8/s-korea-logs-record-jump-in-daily-covid-cases-eyes-tougher-curbs (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 75 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 2,462. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2145459/record-75-covid-deaths-7-058-new-cases (''Bangkok Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Hanoi]] suspends all [[public transport]] services to and from 14 [[Provinces of Vietnam|province]]s impacted by the COVID-19 outbreak and urges people to [[Stay-at-home order|stay at home]] after the country reports a record 1,314 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/vietnam-capital-announces-movement-curbs-after-record-covid-19-cases-2021-07-08/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] surpasses 30,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://hungarytoday.hu/coronavirus-hungary-july-8-thursday-deaths-new-cases/ (Hungary Today)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Luxembourg]]
****[[Luxembourg]] [[Prime Minister of Luxembourg|Prime Minister]] [[Xavier Bettel]] is discharged from hospital after being in a serious but stable condition due to COVID-19 for several days. Bettel thanks the medical services and announces that he will resume activities through telework until the end of his isolation period. [https://today.rtl.lu/news/luxembourg/a/1751720.html (RTL)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 32,551 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 5,022,893. [https://www.itv.com/news/2021-07-08/uk-covid-cases-rise-by-32551-in-a-day-as-death-toll-increases-by-35 (ITV News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nigeria]]
***[[Nigeria]] reports its first case of the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant in a traveller following the routine travel test required of all international travellers and genomic sequencing at the [[Nigeria Centre for Disease Control|NCDC]] National Reference Laboratory, [[Abuja]]. [https://allafrica.com/stories/202107090029.html (AllAfrica)]
**The global death toll from [[COVID-19]] surpasses 4 million. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/07/07/world/global-covid-death-toll-4-million-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–European Union relations]]
**The [[European Parliament]] votes 578–29 to pass a 28-point nonbinding resolution condemning the tightening restrictions on the press in [[Hong Kong]] following the shutdown of the [[Pro-democracy camp (Hong Kong)|pro-democracy]] tabloid ''[[Apple Daily]]''. The resolution also calls for the [[European Commission]] to take punitive actions in response, such as sanctioning officials responsible for drafting and enforcing the [[2020 Hong Kong national security law|national security law]], and refusing invitations to the [[2022 Winter Olympics|Beijing Winter Olympics]] next year. [https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3140391/european-parliament-adopts-resolution-hong-kong-press-freedom?module=lead_hero_story_2&pgtype=homepage (''South China Morning Post'')]
*[[2019 Bolivian political crisis]]
**[[Bolivia]] accuses [[Argentina]] of providing weaponry to the military and police of Bolivia during the [[2019 Senkata and Sacaba Massacres]]. The Bolivian government also accuses former [[president of Argentina]] [[Mauricio Macri]] of wanting the assassination of [[Evo Morales]] during his ousting. Argentina was among the first countries to recognize the interim presidency of [[Jeanine Áñez]] in 2019. [https://www.a24.com/politica/bolivia-denuncia-que-mauricio-macri-apoyo-el-golpe-estado-ese-pais-equipamiento-n845798 (A24)]
*[[Uruguay]]an Foreign Minister [[Francisco Bustillo]] announces that his country will continue to negotiate with third parties or blocks independent of the [[MERCOSUR]] bloc, including extending preferential tariffs to other countries even if doing so contradicts the bloc's consensuses. [[President of Uruguay|President]] [[Luis Lacalle Pou]], while calling for the bloc to be reformed, states that Uruguay will still remain a full member of the bloc. [https://en.mercopress.com/2021/07/08/uruguay-swears-allegiance-to-mercosur-but-will-negotiate-independently-with-third-countries (MercoPress)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020–2021 Belarusian protests#Attacks on journalists and censorship|Belarusian attacks on journalists and censorship]]
**Belarusian authorities block the website of ''[[Nasha Niva]]'' and detains two of the newspaper's journalists. The journalists' apartments are also searched by authorities. A spokesman for the website said that it is the latest crackdown on democracy activists and independent journalism in the country, conducted in the "worst way of the Soviet era". [https://apnews.com/article/belarus-government-europe-belarus-media-business-495db119522b25dac6d8351fdb37f1f5 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Samoan constitutional crisis]]
**The [[Faatuatua i le Atua Samoa ua Tasi]] party asks the [[Supreme Court of Samoa|Supreme Court]] to recognize the impromptu swearing-in of newly elected officials because, according to party leader [[Naomi Mataʻafa]], all other venues were blocked when her party was locked out of [[Parliament of Samoa|Parliament]]. The Supreme Court had earlier rejected a similar petition but had granted a review. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/446433/fast-to-ask-samoa-judges-to-recognise-impromptu-swearing-in (RNZ)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2020 Summer Olympics]], [[2020 Summer Paralympics]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**The [[Tokyo Organising Committee of the Olympic and Paralympic Games]] announce that the games will be held without spectators following a state of emergency declared in the [[Tokyo]] area beginning on July 12 following an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases in the Japanese capital. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-57760883 (BBC News)]
